description: A set of four nearly parallel, low‐relief linear ridges trending NW–SE, each approximately 20–30 m apart and 200–300 m in length. These ridges appear as positive slope breaks in the hillshade and subtle convex curvature in the DTM. In the NIR image they register as moisture‐retentive dark lines, and in the true‐color composite exhibit darker, more vigourous canopy—consistent with anthropogenic ‘terra preta’ soils along embanked raised‐field beds.

A sinuous channel‐like depression connecting the parallel ridges, oriented roughly N–S and curving gently with local microtopography. It is visible as a concave slope in the DTM, a subtle negative curvature line in the hillshade, and as a high‐reflectance (bright) strip in the NIR—suggesting standing or slow‐draining water. The feature is not present in the OSM roads or drainage network, implying an ancient engineered conduit or drainage ditch.
